title: Floquet framework for driven polar quantum systems
authors: Viktor Novičenko, Piotr Gładysz, Karolina Słowik, Egidijus Anisimovas
abstract: We present an analytical and numerical Floquet treatment of a driven polar two-level quantum system characterized by both longitudinal and transverse coupling to a periodic field. Analytically, we derive a dressed-frame effective Hamiltonian up to first order in the inverse driving frequency, incorporating the longitudinal coupling nonperturbatively. This yields closed expressions for the effective transverse coupling strength and the effective detuning, both of which are modified by the presence of the longitudinal interaction. In the nonpolar limit, these expressions recover the usual near-resonant Rabi coupling and the Bloch-Siegert shift. As a second main result, we develop a numerical flow-equation framework that yields a time-independent effective Hamiltonian across a broad range of transverse and longitudinal coupling strengths. This dual framework is relevant for a variety of platforms, including driven polar quantum systems, optical lattices, superconducting circuits, and solids subject to surface acoustic waves.
summary: The paper develops and compares two advanced methods—analytical high-frequency expansion and numerical flow equations—to find the effective Hamiltonian for a driven polar quantum system. It successfully handles complex interactions by treating longitudinal coupling nonperturbatively, providing accurate predictions across various coupling regimes relevant to modern quantum hardware.
main_problem: The paper addresses developing a Floquet treatment for a driven polar two-level quantum system subjected to both longitudinal and transverse coupling from a periodic field.
main_result: A dual framework combining analytical high-frequency expansions with numerical flow equations successfully yields the time-independent effective Hamiltonian, even when longitudinal couplings are strong.
method: The authors employ Floquet theory, utilizing an analytical expansion (up to first order in $\omega^{-1}$) and a numerical flow-equation approach based on continuous block diagonalization.
model_or_system: The system is a driven two-level quantum system characterized by a Hamiltonian involving longitudinal ($g_z$) and transverse ($g_x$) coupling strengths modulated periodically by the driving frequency ($\omega$).
key_observables: Effective transverse coupling strength, effective detuning, time evolution operator ($\hat{U}_{	ext{eff}}$), and reconstructed micromotion components.
important_parameters: Driving frequency ($\omega$), longitudinal coupling ($g_z$), transverse coupling ($g_x$), and the ratio $g_x/\omega$.
main_assumptions: The analytical method relies on a high-frequency expansion in $\omega^{-1}$, while the numerical flow approach requires truncation of the harmonic series.
figures_summary: Figures compare convergence of harmonic weights, validate the zeroth-plus-first-order expansion against numerical results, and show agreement between direct integration, flow-equation, and analytical effective Hamiltonians across various coupling regimes.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical model and Hamiltonian. It then details the analytical derivation using dressing transformations and high-frequency expansions. Subsequently, it presents the complementary numerical flow-equation framework for calculating the time-independent effective Hamiltonian, culminating in comparisons between both methods.
why_interesting: This work provides a robust theoretical toolkit to analyze driven quantum systems where standard approximations fail due to strong coupling terms ($g_z \sim \omega$), making it highly relevant for trapped ion or superconducting circuit platforms.
